instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/tests/pages.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Fix the test setup only. Keep every assertion's intent: do not delete, skip or loosen an expectation to make it pass. If a test still fails after its setup is right, leave the assertion as it is.

1. `openMenu`: the selector ends in `,[aria-haspopup]`, so querySelector returns the first tab's menu trigger whichever page is asked for. That is why `delete an empty page` fails with `expected [ 'id5' ] to deeply equal [ 'default' ]`, `delete asks with elements` with `expected [ 'id7' ] to deeply equal [ 'default' ]`, and `reorder by menu` at line 267 with `expected false to be true`. Query only `[data-testid="page-tab-menu-${pageId}"]`. `menuItem` also reuses a menu already open for another page: make sure the menu open is the requested page's (PageTabs closes it on a second click of the same trigger).

2. `describe("pages (scene scope)")` renders `<Excalidraw />` without handleKeyboardGlobally, so Keyboard.undo and Keyboard.redo never reach the editor. `undo stays on its page` (line 361), `stack survives a switch` (line 382) and `deleting a page discards its stack` (line 399) fail with `expected false to be true`. Render it with `handleKeyboardGlobally={true}`, as the `pages (paste)` block does.

3. `text edit commits on switch`: `const second = createPage()` activates the new page by default, so the text is typed on `second` and `switchTo(second)` does nothing; fails at line 347 with the text still in h.elements. Use `createPage({ activate: false })`.

4. `render scope` fails at line 316: `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'B' ]`. B sits at (500, 500), which is probably outside the jsdom viewport, and h.app.visibleElements only holds what is on screen. Keep the assertion that B is visible and A is not; put B where the viewport can see it, and let the render settle if needed.

5. `paste lands on the active page` (line 513, `expected +0 to be 1`) with an unhandled rejection: `TypeError: this.app.ownerDocument.elementFromPoint is not a function` at App.clipboard.ts:331. jsdom has no elementFromPoint: define it for this test file the way the repo's clipboard test does.

6. yarn test:typecheck: packages/excalidraw/tests/pages.test.tsx(529,46) and (564,46): error TS2322: `index` is `string`, not assignable to `FractionalIndex`. Cast the fixture's index values to FractionalIndex.

instruction:
Fix `excalidraw-app/tests/pages.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. The helper at line 130 is `const createPage = (name: string) => act(() => h.app.pages.createPage({ name, activate: false }));`. act() returns a thenable, not the callback's value, so `second` is a Promise and `second.id` is undefined. That is the cause of the TS2339 errors below and of three failures: `active page stays local when a remote page list arrives` (expected 'default' to be undefined at line 302), `cursors follow the page` (expected [ 'missing', 'other', 'same' ] to deeply equal [ 'missing', 'same' ] at line 380) and `page records hold no viewport` (expected 0 to be greater than 0 at line 392). Make the helper synchronous: assign the page to a local inside the act callback and return it. Keep every assertion. If one still fails with the real id, leave the assertion as it is.
